why_how.text: Traffic approaching a school bus stopped for loading or unloading generally must stop. With a dividing median, opposite-side traffic is excepted, while traffic following or beside the bus in its direction must stop.
After stopping for a school bus, wait until it resumes moving or deactivates the warnings, and until all passengers loading or unloading have cleared the roadway.
Large trucks are longer, heavier and harder to maneuver than cars and require additional room for turning.
The handbook calls a truck or bus's enlarged blind areas the no-zones, including areas beside, behind and in front of it.
Before towing, use suitable equipment, stay within the towing capacity, distribute weight appropriately and secure the load.
Inspect and maintain both tow vehicle and trailer, become familiar with handling through practice, and consider tow mirrors or other needed safety equipment.
Allow time when trailering and remain calm if control is lost; the handbook's brief checklist is not a complete towing procedure.

why_how.text: A truck or bus has large blind areas on both sides. If its driver's face is not visible in the side mirror, do not assume the driver can see your vehicle.
The right-side blind area is especially hazardous because large vehicles may need a wide right turn.
Avoid following closely in a large vehicle's rear blind area; you may be unseen and unable to see traffic conditions ahead of it.
Large vehicles need extra stopping room. Do not merge closely in front of a truck or bus and then reduce speed.
Before moving into the lane ahead of a truck or bus, make sure its entire front is visible in your rearview mirror.
Give a commercial vehicle ample space during highway entry and merging, and avoid cutting it off, tailgating or speeding around it.
